On 2023/05/21 we discussed wolf hunting methods: pursuit (endurance chasing), ambush, pack/cooperative hunting, stealth stalking, and opportunistic scavenging of carrion or small prey. #wolves #hunting

Wolf prey choice is based on availability, not preference: elk, deer, bison, moose, caribou, plus smaller animals (rabbits, rodents, birds, hares, voles) when large prey is scarce; depends on pack size, food availability, and season. #wolves #prey
Wolves can hunt alone but solo hunts are less successful and riskier; alone they mostly target smaller/weaker prey. Pack life is central to their social behavior. #wolves #hunting
No evidence of vegetarian wolves: their digestive system is specialized for meat; vegetation (fruits, berries, grasses) is only a minor supplemental nutrient source. #wolves #diet

Pack hunting coordination in wolves: vocal/gesture/scent communication to plan, coordinated pursuit and turning of prey, ambush positions, division of labor by individual strengths, and sharing meat after the kill. #wolves #pack-hunting
After a wolf kill, feeding order is not strictly fixed: alpha pair usually eat first but prey size, pack size, social rank, and individual personality all affect who eats when. #wolves #feeding

Wolf pack conflicts over food or hunting roles (growling, snarling, biting) are usually resolved via dominance/submission signals and posturing; dominant wolves lead hunts and eat first, lower-ranking ones submit, so serious injury is rare. #wolves #conflict

Topic modeling identifies latent topics/themes in a text corpus. Most common method is Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model where each document is a mixture of topics and each topic a distribution over words. Alternatives: NMF (Non-negative Matrix Factorization), PLSA (Probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis), and CTM (Correlated Topic Model). #nlp #topic_modeling

Topic modeling identifies latent topics/themes in a text corpus; the most common method is Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model where each document is a mixture of topics and each topic a distribution over words. #nlp #topic_modeling
Topic modeling methods other than LDA: NMF (Non-negative Matrix Factorization), PLSA (Probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis), and CTM (Correlated Topic Model). #nlp #topic_modeling

TF-IDF = Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency, a numerical statistic reflecting a word's importance in a document/corpus. TF normalizes term count by document length; IDF is the log of total documents divided by documents containing the term, so rare words get more weight; the score is TF times IDF. #nlp #tfidf
TF-IDF is a feature-extraction/text-representation technique used in text classification, information retrieval, and document clustering — not a topic modeling technique. #nlp #tfidf

TF-IDF vs bag of words: both turn documents into numerical vectors, but bag of words only counts word occurrences, while TF-IDF weights terms by within-document frequency (TF) and corpus-wide rarity (IDF), upweighting terms important to a specific document and downweighting terms common across all documents. #nlp #tfidf
